source.title: Where Does Benjamin Netanyahu Go from Here?
source.note: published 10-28 23:20 UTC; in the 10-29 sweep (matched on 'iran' — the word is in the dek only). Filed 10-29 as a sighting (see-fp-1028-netanyahu-regime), not cut — the Doran podcast page was the day's FP cut. Cut 10-30 as a beta lede: no 10-30 sweep at run time; the RP corner had nothing fuller in the 10-29 queue (Shapiro ×2 owed, TCN and Kirk 0 hits; Douthat on the slate, not the object). Read to the wall via the cloud fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over twelve words. ~233 visible body words. My call: a second FP beta on the force in two days, from the other FP author; flagged

object.label: the next offensive against Iran — the force (slate01; PG01 §5, the war that made the crunch): read by the RP corner's Israel correspondent through the Israeli result — Netanyahu's bloc 53, Eisenkot 48, the Arab parties 19 of 120, no bloc at 61 — as 'just well enough for his highest priority: bringing down the Iranian regime' (dek). lines.quote: where does Benjamin Netanyahu go from here?
lines.note: THE HEADLINE: a question about the holder's ally, not about the force; the object absent from the hed
lines.zWhy: a prime minister with nowhere to go reads slightly against a strike that needs him

lines.quote: Netanyahu did not win on Tuesday; in pure mathematical terms, he crashed
lines.note: the dek's first two sentences: the result, dated, with 'crashed' as its size
lines.zWhy: a lost vote reads neither way on the force until the dek's third sentence

lines.quote: he may have done just well enough for his highest priority: bringing down the Iranian regime
lines.note: THE OBJECT, ONCE — the strike pre-credited to a vote that produced no government; 'highest priority' is the goal stated as settled, undated, no order; the Doran page's 'inevitable' (fp 10-29) from the Israeli side
lines.zWhy: a result sufficient for the regime's fall is the force not relenting

lines.quote: you asked the people of Israel one simple question, and they can't give you an answer
lines.note: the joke — the corner reading the electorate's indecision; the object absent; vacancy
lines.zWhy: an electorate without an answer reads neither way on the force

lines.quote: Netanyahu's coalition 53 of 120, Eisenkot's bloc 48, the two Arab parties 19; none at the 61 majority
lines.note: THE RECORD — the seat count, the page's lowest line; the vote's record, not the force's
lines.zWhy: a seat count reads neither way on the force

lines.quote: Israelis vote for a party; the parties negotiate a majority; a coalition needs 61 and then votes in a government
lines.note: the mechanism explained for a US reader — the right domain, the vote's plane
lines.zWhy: a coalition rule reads neither way on the force

lines.quote: a minority government needs the Arab parties to abstain, which they won't; so he must pull people over from Eisenkot's coalition
lines.note: the author's path: no majority without defectors — the condition for the dek's 'well enough', unstated as such
lines.zWhy: a government not yet formed reads neither way on the force

lines.quote: and there the chaos math begins
lines.note: the page's peak and the wall — 'chaos math' is the arithmetic given a temperament; cuts to 'Read more'; vacancy
lines.zWhy: chaos reads neither way on the force
